prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to remove chosen proteins

statement.case_for: After the full first round I still hold B011 as my final position. It passes my test of a game-changer: a new idea that is chemically simple (a molecule that joins a ligase to a target), that other groups have reproduced widely, and that lets a small molecule do something an inhibitor cannot, namely remove the protein. Crews and Deshaies established the concept in 2001, and Crews carried it for two decades. Ciulli's VHL ligands and his ternary-complex structural work turned it into a design discipline that others now apply. That supports a clean three-name attribution to a single, definable achievement, which the chair asked for. I therefore define the citation narrowly, around bifunctional degraders that recruit E3 ligases, and I do not claim the cereblon molecular-glue mechanism, which is a related but separate discovery. The first round also showed that this configuration is not an outlier. Two of us propose it, and five more name B011 as an alternative or second choice.
statement.case_against: The main reservation, which Aili and I both raised and the chair repeated, is timing. As far as I know no degrader has yet been approved, and I have no current regulatory evidence to settle this. If the committee judges that a prize needs an approved medicine, B011 is early. Second, a narrow citation leaves Handa, Ito and Gray outside, and a reader may see that as slighting the work that explained how thalidomide acts. I accept that cost, because a citation covering both PROTACs and glues would not be a single achievement and could not be held to three names. Third, I have to concede that the base-editing case is mature in the same sense and no less mature than mine, so I cannot use maturity to rank B007 below B011 and have to rest the choice on attribution and breadth.

responses.point: As chair, Linke asked whether base editing can be framed as distinct from the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether it holds at three names (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) given Target-AID, and he holds B007 as his first choice on a clear, explainable deaminase principle.
responses.response: I accept the distinctness argument. Replacing cleavage with deaminase chemistry, and evolving TadA so that adenine editing works at all, is a different chemical invention from the nuclease. My difficulty is the attribution. Komor and Gaudelli did the founding experiments, but Kondo and Nishida reported a parallel cytidine editor, and a three-name citation has to exclude them. For that reason I keep B007 as my first alternative and not my first choice. If the committee settles the Target-AID priority from the dates, I would move toward B007, and I would prefer Liu, Komor and Gaudelli to Somfai's Liu-only option.

responses.point: Somfai proposes a two-part prize, B065 for Buchwald and Hartwig and B007 for Liu alone, and himself concedes that B065 had thin opening support and that the two parts share no theme.
responses.response: I do not support the two-part form here. A prize that pairs C-N coupling with a Liu-only base-editing part leaves out the lead inventors of both editor classes, and it has no common thread that we could explain to a general audience. The chair's question about pairings has a real answer only if the two parts share a theme, and these do not. On B065 itself, I agree that C-N coupling is useful and mature, but I see it as an extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize, with the unresolved Kosugi priority question, and I do not think it is a game-changer in the sense I use.

responses.point: Aili also proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for B011, but treats the opening breadth (ranked by all eight) as acceptance and not as merit, and sees the molecular-glue and cereblon strand as having the stronger mechanistic payoff.
responses.response: I agree on the trio and on not treating breadth as merit, and I restate my reason: it is merit that decides, and I judge the PROTAC design principle by its generality and its reproduction by independent groups. On the glue strand I agree it is a decisive mechanism, but a claim about how thalidomide works is a different achievement from a design rule for bifunctional molecules. Treating them as one would produce a six-name citation. The chair's question about which three to name has my answer: Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, with the citation worded around designed recruitment of E3 ligases.

responses.point: Brzezinski is the only member to propose nitrogenase (B028) with Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, and acknowledges that the N2 binding mode is unresolved and that Dean and Ribbe are an attribution risk.
responses.response: The chair asked whether the unresolved binding mode is a barrier to citing mechanism, and I think it is. The FeMo-cofactor structure with its central carbide is a great result, but a citation could honestly state only the structure, and the three-name list would still leave out Dean and Ribbe, whose biosynthesis and genetics work is central. My game-changer test asks for a new capability with consequences, and nitrogenase has not yet given one. I respect the chemistry and have not changed my view of the ranking, but his answer on what a one-sentence citation could say would still be useful to me.

responses.point: Sparr proposes biomolecular phase separation (B046) with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as a physical-chemical organising principle, and names the in vivo relevance debate and the Pappu and Mittag credit as open.
responses.response: This answers the chair's question for B046. A citation can reward the physical principle and the founding experiments without endorsing any specific cellular condensate, but I doubt it can be written to avoid that, since the principle's interest comes from its role in cells. Criteria for what is a functional condensate are still disputed, and the credit between Rosen and Pappu and Mittag is not clean. I regard it as chemistry, but too early. I would revisit it in a few years.

uncertainties: Whether any PROTAC or molecular-glue degrader has been approved or is close to approval. I do not know the current regulatory status, and it decides whether B011 is early.
Whether the committee will accept a narrow citation around designed bifunctional degraders and leave the cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) unnamed without it reading as an omission.
The Target-AID priority question for B007. If the dates show Kondo and Nishida were independent and not later, my objection to a Liu, Komor and Gaudelli trio would weaken.
Whether my theory background makes me discount B026 too heavily or too lightly; I keep it only as an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: No recusal issue is apparent for B011. My connection to Arieh Warshel and my work on free-energy and EVB simulation lie close to B026 and B018, which is why B026 appears only as an alternative. I have no personal or institutional link to Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Liu, Komor, Gaudelli, Buchwald, Hartwig or the other shortlisted names. Nothing in round 1 changes this disclosure.
